source_review: Only the periodic native caller gains lake=self.lake, and the public scheduler wrapper retains its None return. Built-in patterns use the new helper; GC and the explicit custom script retain their separate execution paths.
Whole-batch pattern validation, bounded per-task candidate discovery, no-follow directory access and regular single-link leaf identity checks precede confirmed unlink accounting.

The per-task effect guard is reused. A fresh existing-only read-only catalog checks agreed closed lifecycle and all current attempt phases; stop/effect HOLD and conflicting/unavailable authority do not downgrade to legacy.
Actual routed database and sidecars, framework-private trees, current configured paths and native launch-bound output/control roots are protected.

Actual cleanup.script, post_scripts[].script, pre_script, sealed_hashes, evaluation_bundle.files, selected config and report source paths are accounted for. Pro-owned state, quotas, results and manifests remain under protected control roots; no additional Pro run_cleanup caller exists.

The final narrow correction adds tree-aware protection for task-relative model_lineage.artifact and eval_checkpoint, plus project-relative resume.immutable_inputs. It does not read large model or input bodies.
The pre-existing scratch.json/scratch.log disposable contract remains covered by the unchanged orphan cleanup test. No blanket JSON/log/checkpoint-extension exemption was introduced.

The final contract is consistent with the implementation's bounded guarantees and explicitly excludes standalone GC, cold-storage movement, custom cleanup programs, Pro process control and natural-exit descendant closure.
evidence_limits: No GPU, provider, live process signal or holdout access was used.
The helper coordinates cooperating framework writers; it is not a sandbox or an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction.
Only confirmed unlinks increment deletion counts; an I/O error after unlink can leave a removed file without a success count. No rollback or recoverable trash guarantee is claimed.

The root's interrupted candidate full suites are not counted as product failures here. Final full-suite and paired-test results belong to the root aggregate; this report claims only the actual independent targeted run above.
No GC/director implementation or tests were included in this C1 review.
